2:_: There is not in the breach 4 tefachim. It is possible he speaks of a courtyard wide in the middle and at the end it is narrow so that in its full width there is not 4 tefachim; but if the entire courtyard is less than 4 tefachim no repair is needed as written in seif 28:
3:א: All that it is. Even less than a finger (Beit Yosef, Bach):
3:ב: One tied a person there. And it requires study — for in siman 362 seif 5 it says regarding a person he need not be tied, and one must say he speaks where they did not inform him that they placed it for lechi — if so he will certainly leave and not stand there all day, therefore it requires being tied:
5:_: Cannot stand. And even if the wind does not knock it down but only shakes it as written at the beginning of siman 362: thus an incident where Yom Tov fell on the 6th day and the eruv was lost on the 5th day, and Maharik permitted because on Yom Tov one must also make eruv for things without any need for Yom Tov — for we say since it was permitted for Yom Tov, etc., end of his words; and it appears to me one should not rely on this — nevertheless if two days of Yom Tov fell on the 5th and 6th days, then the 1st day is chol and it is not applicable to say since it was permitted it was permitted; rather even the first Yom Tov on the 6th day is forbidden, for perhaps Yom Tov and Shabbat are two sanctities as written siman 416 seif 2; see siman 365 seif 7:
6:_: Distant from the wall. For the air of this side comes and nullifies it (R' Yitzchak) — therefore if the lechi is wider than 3 it is permitted since the standing exceeds the breach (Shach, Riaz) see siman 362 seif 9; but the view of Tosafos is that even so it is forbidden see seif 34:
7:_: Even fragments. Stones protruding from the fence one above the other less than 3 constitute a lechi (Gemara 4:15):
8:_: From asheirah wood. And we do not say crushing diminishes its measure as written siman 316, for lechi also requires some measure of height and width, since it requires only a small measure the Sages were not strict (Tosafos 4:80), and see there further, and see in Maggid Mishneh and siman 372 seif 15:
11:א: Even if he did not make it. For lechi is by reason of partition, and a partition standing by itself is valid:
11:ב: As if they leaned on it. Even though they did not lean on it explicitly (Hagahot Alfasi) — it appears that if explicitly they did not lean — such as they did not carry on the previous Shabbat through this lechi — it is not a lechi, and so is in Rashba whom Rabbenu Yosef brought:
12:א: 4 amot. For 4 amot is the measure of a mavo and there is no recognition — even though lechi is by reason of partition, nevertheless some recognition is required; but if the mavo is 8 amot wide it is permitted by standing as breached:
12:ב: He placed it. But leaning on it does not help, not as Rabbenu Yosef, and so too in Taz in the name of a great one:
13:א: The lechi that extends. As written in the gloss: a mavo paved with lechayim less than less than 3, and the paving is 4 amot in the length of the mavo — another lechi is needed to permit the entire mavo, end of his words; nevertheless if visible from outside and equal inside, or the reverse, it is judged as lechi — see in the Gemara and Rashi:
13:ב: With its end. For the other side is shorter than this, and see s.k. 30 and siman 365 seif 4; and in the Gemara he speaks where his other side is also long, as explained in the difficulty above:
13:ג: And it is forbidden to use. Even if placed for lechi (Tosafos):
15:_: From erev Shabbat it is invalid. For korah is by reason of recognition, and when he did not make it for that purpose there is no recognition:
17:_: To receive a brick. And if the mavo is 10 amot wide it must receive 18 bricks which is 9 amot, and with two mashehuin it suffices for the length of the korah, and from its two ends we say lavud as written in seif 21, and so too:
21:_: And it does not touch. And even if distant from the two walls we say lavud:
22:_: Within a tefach. And even if together they are 4 tefachim — if the air between them is more than a tefach it does not help, for in any case it is not fit to place a brick on them, unlike in seif 17 where it is fit only that they are not strong, as explained above, not as I understood:
23:_: And there are those who disqualify. For he holds as the first view in seif 22:
24:_: And it extends somewhat, etc. Meaning it extends downward somewhat more than 10 from where it begins — if so it would be a partition and invalid both as korah and as partition too, for a partition is suspended — it teaches us it is valid; against Bach:
25:_: Valid when they are. For we say chavit and lavud — even though for a korah of a tefach even if higher than 3 we say chavit, here is different since korah is over a mavo (Tosafos):
26:א: Spaced. The measure of spacing is more than constricted — half a finger per amah (Maggid Mishneh, Peri Megadim):
26:ב: Except with tzurat hapetach. And Rambam wrote that less than 4 amot its law is as a courtyard, and it is possible he did not mean tzurat hapetach specifically:
26:ג: In a wide building. And the same with earth, and one must be careful when trampled by feet that it not diminish from the measure:
26:ד: Two courtyards, etc. For whenever there is not abundance of residents they use it discreetly and require more partition (Beit Yosef, Rashba), and if so it is possible to be lenient in our mavo'ot since there is abundance of residents, and it is possible they did not distinguish in a mavo:
26:ה: And there are those who disagree. Since they can make eruv together through the openings they are considered as one courtyard, and the same regarding houses open to each other:
26:ו: The law of courtyards. Since most cities are surrounded by a wall in settlement and afterward enclosed — one should apply the law of a courtyard and repair the mavo'ot (between Jews and gentiles) as one who comes to divide a courtyard into 3 and 4 domains if there were small paths in the courtyard between house and house requiring tzurat hapetach or two pasin of two mashehuin as in Hagahot Maimoniyot in the name of Maharam, end of his words Terumat HaDeshen — and if the mavo is not 10 amot wide, two pasin of mashehu suffice, and so Mahariv in his laws siman 18: in Hagahot Maimoniyot Maharam explained that our mavo'ot need only two lechayim for they are only removal of residents and do not need tzurat hapetach; nevertheless it appears our mavo'ot are not in their category as open to reshut harabbim to require tzurat hapetach in their crookedness as an crooked mavo — there he speaks of open to reshut harabbim, end of his words; and it is obvious he speaks in what is surrounded by a wall, for he wrote it is only removal of residents; but in unwalled cities tzurat hapetach is needed as written siman 364 regarding open to karmelis see seif 3 that even in its crookedness repair is needed, for there is no difference between reshut harabbim and karmelis, and so Beit Yosef there in the name of responsum of Ran, and so Mishna Berurah siman 392 — except that Mahariv's words were inclined to another view see there, and it requires study that I did not see practiced thus, and therefore it appears to me that since stam Rama wrote all our mavo'ot have the law of courtyards — it implies even without a surrounding wall, since houses and courtyards are not open into them they have the law of a courtyard, and in a courtyard there is no difference between crooked and straight — only one repair at its head is needed; nevertheless for this that is called mavo, if it has no wall tzurat hapetach is needed since they are close to reshut harabbim as Semak wrote; but its crooked part is not close to reshut harabbim and does not need repair, end of his words in the gloss; and see siman 364 that on the second side lechi suffices, and in Levush Aharon: and Maharil in responsum 160 wrote our cities where gentiles dwell within have the law of karmelis, and even utensils that rested within are forbidden to carry outside 4 amot, etc., see there, and so in his derashot; but we have only Shulchan Aruch's words who wrote siman 357 and siman 365 that they have the law of courtyards, and if breaches were made in the wall see siman 365 seif 3 and siman 372:
26:ז: Two reeds. On the ground, but the walls of the mavo are not counted in place of the reeds — for otherwise why was a korah a tefach wide needed, for in all that it is there is tzurat hapetach; rather reeds must be placed, and one can say what he wrote in Sukkah that one places a reed on the walls and need not a reed from here — see siman 631 seif 3; and it is possible this is a mere stringency to make tzurat hapetach, and it appears to me if there is a protruding pillar in the wall it is judged as a reed, for it is no worse than lechi in seif 11:
28:_: That there is not in its width, etc. Meaning its opening is not 3 wide even if inside it is very wide:
29:א: A mavo whose side, etc. It appears here that the sea is considered a partition — and it requires study, for Tosafos 22b wrote: and one might say one cannot make reshut hayachid since mountains surround it, and in Do not make reshut hayachid that surrounds it is a river Diglat — and some say a partition not made by man is not considered a partition and many come and nullify their partition, end of his words; see end of this siman, and one must say here he speaks where ships do not pass there to the port, for there the sea itself is a partition, and the same for other waters where ships do not pass — they themselves are a partition as written siman 356 and so in the Gemara 24b and Tosafos one does not make, etc., that the river itself is a partition, and so in Aruch entry Ozel; and per what is written siman 358 specifically when the riverbank is 10 deep, and so Rashi and Rivash here — but if the riverbank is a slope and when one walks the slope is still not 10 high it is not a partition, as written in this siman:
29:ב: Lest the sea rise with a sandbar. For such is the way of the sea that it shortens and becomes land the width of a parsah and partitions are nullified and they also carry in mavo'ot as at first (Rashi); and in Maggid Mishneh it appears that even if the sea shortens nevertheless a slope 10 deep remains as a partition, except the concern is lest they carry from the mavo to the place where the sea dried which is karmelis — even if surrounded by the sea's partition — for it was not enclosed for residence as written siman 365 seif 3; but when the sea exists there is no concern since the sea is not carried together with the mavo, end of his words; and if so for us complete partitions are needed on the sea side, and tzurat hapetach or lechi or korah does not help as Ameimar did who ruled against Rashi's view, and Tur holds as Rashi's view — if so repair of the rest of the mavo suffices; and it appears from Rashi's and Rosh's and Tur's words that regarding other rivers we are not concerned lest a sandbar rise, as in Tosafos 24 see there; and know that in any case the river must be literally adjacent to the head of the mavo, but if distant from the houses 10 amot repair is needed for that place is breached, and so in Tosafos 24 in the words let him make tzurat hapetach, etc., and in the words let him make lechi, etc., see there: Constantinople even though breached to the sea in several places more than 10 — it is as closed (R' Yehuda the Castilian 94, and so seif 92) see siman 415 seif 6; and in Rivash siman 415 he wrote: a mavo open to karmelis needs tzurat hapetach, and that one whose side was sea was not open at both ends for it had 3 partitions except on two sides there was a small breach on one side to the sea and on one side to refuse, and the sea bank was 10 deep, etc., end of his words; but the implication of the poskim appears that even fully open to the sea is permitted, and above siman 364; and if so in our rivers whose way is to dry in summer the 4th [season] one should forbid see siman 365 seif 3: thus the Yerushalmi 18:4 — mavo'ot open to the sea are as open to a valley, and the law of the alley of R' Chiya — he need not tzurat hapetach for it is as collected 10 from within 3; know that if they freeze in rainy season the partition is nullified and it is forbidden to carry:
30:_: One side long. And even lechayim do not help against the long side, as in Beit Yosef, and so R' Levi Chaviv siman 66, and Bach wrote that lechayim help:
31:א: And they did not make. Since they did not make and cannot carry in the mavo they do not forbid the inner part:
31:ב: Two pasin. For even one courtyard can divide thus (Rosh), and a city surrounded by a wall with doors fit to be locked except at one opening — that opening does not detract from lechi or korah and the entire city is like one mavo that has lechi at its head and one does not make eruv for half of it; and if there is a breach the qualification is nullified (and see siman 365 seif 2) and one may qualify half and leave half (Beit Yosef siman 364 in the name of Rivash):
33:א: A pas 4 wide. But less than that does not help even if each side is less than 10, for the air of this side and that side comes and nullifies it as written seif 4:
33:ב: And some say there is not, etc. Beit Yosef questioned this, for we rule in siman 364 seif 3 that even if there is not 10 in its crookedness it is as open — one must say the Tur holds it is different here since both openings are on one side he will not go around the pas, as Ritva wrote see there; but regarding more than 10 the Tur does not hold as Ritva, and nevertheless the main thing is as the early authorities, as in Bach:
34:א: A pas wide, etc. And lechi is also needed for the mavo, for a pas does not help since it is distant 3 from the wall (Tosafos, and so R' Yitzchak), and see s.k. 6:
34:ב: That they not leave. But stam we are not concerned they will go through a small opening that does not diminish walking thus, unlike in siman 365 where it is from the side and they shorten their path we are concerned for this (Gemara):
36:א: And with this he began, etc. And if the entire city is surrounded by a mound and afterward they built houses in it — it is forbidden as written siman 358 seif 2 see seif 8:
36:ב: It is as a partition. And per what is written in seif 29 in the name of Tosafos — one must say that many do not pass through it, for otherwise many come and nullify the partition since it is not made by man; and it is possible it is not called many unless less than 600,000, as written siman 358 seif 6, and so is the view of the poskim who were silent on this:
